related_policies: Common CPT and HCPCS Modifiers, Modifier FY

sections.heading: Overview
content: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has directed providers to use modifier FX to report X-ray services furnished using film. Effective for dates of service beginning January 1, 2017, Original Medicare reimbursement for the technical component (TC) of film X-ray services reported with modifier FX is reduced by 20 percent. The film X-ray reimbursement reduction is required for the Medicare Program by the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2016. Transitioning from film X-ray technology to digital radiography (DR) technology ensures use of the lowest radiation dose necessary to get the image quality needed by providers to make a proper diagnosis. Performing X-rays using DR technology ensures that a patient receives the highest standard of care as established by professional societies and regulatory agencies and helps reduce a patient’s lifetime exposure to potentially cancer-causing medical radiation. Humana works to reduce our members’ exposure to medical radiation. Directly and through vendor partnerships, we educate our members on the risks of medical radiation exposure and encourage our in-network providers to provide high quality advanced diagnostic services that meet a broad set of industry standards.

sections.heading: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana plans require providers to follow the appropriate Medicare Program guidance for correct coding using modifier FX . Providers must append modifier FX to a procedure code for an X-ray service furnished using film. The requirement applies to a TC - only charge and to a global charge for such a service. Humana reduces reimbursement for the TC of such services by 20 percent for dates of service beginning January 1, 2017. The reduction applies to the TC of a TC -only charge and to the TC of a global charge for such a service.

sections.heading: Definitions of Italicized Terms
content: • Global charge : A global charge is a single charge for both the technical component and the professional component of a service. • Modifier FX : X-Ray taken using film. • Technical component (TC) : The technical component of a service is for all non-physician work and includes administrative, personnel and capital (equipment and facility) costs and related malpractice expenses.
